name: rtx5080
description: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5080 (GB203, Blackwell, sm_120) at its 2295 MHz base clock: one Vortex core per SM.

sources.NUM_CORES, NUM_WARPS, NUM_THREADS, ISSUE: 84 SMs, 48 resident warps/SM, 4 schedulers x 32 lanes (NVIDIA RTX Blackwell GPU Architecture whitepaper, App. B; cudaGetDeviceProperties on an RTX 5080)
sources.DCACHE_SIZE: 128 KB L1/shared per SM (whitepaper App. B)
sources.L2_SIZE, L2_NUM_WAYS: 64 MB L2 (whitepaper App. B); 16 ways as in GPGPU-Sim's Ampere/Hopper L2 configs
sources.L2_NUM_BANKS: 64 banks of 64 B (4 KB/clk): the 48 L2 slices measured by arXiv 2507.10789 deliver about 3.5 KB/clk, nearer 64 banks than 32
sources.DCACHE_MSHR_SIZE, L2_MSHR_SIZE: 384 L1 MSHR entries per SM (24 x 16 banks) and 192 per L2 slice, GPGPU-Sim SM86_RTX3070 (-gpgpu_cache:dl1 A:384:48, dl2 A:192:4)
sources.PLATFORM_MEMORY_NUM_BANKS: 8 x 32-bit GDDR7 devices = 32 independent channels (whitepaper App. B)
sources.PLATFORM_CLOCK_RATE, PLATFORM_MEMORY_PEA: 2295 MHz base clock, 960 GB/s (whitepaper App. B)
sources.reference: Nsight Compute on an RTX 5080 at its 2295 MHz base clock with a cold L2, 2026-10-05. fp32_lanes is the vendor FP32 core count (FP32 FMA lanes per chip, clock-free); dram_bandwidth_gbs the vendor peak. Checked by ci/profile_check.py. l1_hit_cycles comes from an index chase (p = next[p]: an index multiply-add per load), so it sits above ci/profile_check.py's pointer chase (p = *p) by that arithmetic
sources.PLATFORM_MEMORY_TYPE, PLATFORM_MEMORY_DA: 30 Gbps GDDR7 x8 channels modelled as GDDR6 x16 channels at 15000 MT/s: the same channel count, 32 B burst time and 960 GB/s (32 x 2 B x 15 GT/s)
sources.L2_LINK_LATENCY: 137 core cycles each way between an SM and the L2, the SM-to-L2 network, which the L2 bank pipeline (L2_LATENCY) does not model: calibrated with ci/profile_check.py so the SimX pointer chase gives the 354.4-cycle L2 hit latency in 'reference'
sources.PLATFORM_MEMORY_LATENCY: 367 core cycles of PHY/NoC latency beyond the L2 link, calibrated with ci/profile_check.py so the SimX cold pointer chase gives the 802-cycle DRAM latency in 'reference'. Recalibrate when the memory model changes
sources.FETCH_WIDTH: 4 SM processing blocks, each with its own warp scheduler, dispatch unit and L0 instruction cache (NVIDIA RTX Blackwell GPU Architecture whitepaper)
sources.CP_LLC_CLIENT: Host copies reach device memory through the L2 like every other client, so uploaded data is L2-resident at launch
sources.LMEM_NUM_BANKS: 128 B per clock per SM: 32 banks of 4 B on the part (CUDA C++ Programming Guide, shared memory). Vortex banks are XLEN wide (8 B), so 16 banks carry the same bytes per clock; lanes reading one 8 B word share its bank access, so a stride-1 FP32 warp read is conflict-free as on the part
sources.VM_ENABLE, EXT_A_ENABLE, EXT_ZACAS_ENABL: Every NVIDIA GPU since Pascal has a demand-paged MMU (unified memory), global and shared-memory atomics with a native compare-and-swap (atomicCAS), FP16 storage and conversion, and per-partition special-function units for the transcendentals (MUFU)
sources.EXT_TCU_ENABLE, TCU_*, EXT_DXA_ENABLE, E: Fifth-generation tensor cores: FP16/BF16, TF32, FP8, FP4 (NVFP4, MXFP4) and the MX formats, INT8, with 2:4 structured sparsity; no wgmma on sm_120. TMA is the DXA; the fourth-generation RT cores are the RTU (RTX Blackwell whitepaper)
sources.TCU_PE_RATIO: 512 dense FP16 FMA per clock per SM with FP16 accumulation: 225 TFLOPS at the 2617 MHz boost clock over 84 SMs (NVIDIA RTX Blackwell GPU Architecture whitepaper, Appendix B). 4 TCU blocks at NUM_THREADS=32 give 1024 FP16 FMA per clock: ratio 2. The part halves FP16 again when it accumulates in FP32, which the TCU, FP32 accumulator only, does not separate
sources.xlen: 64-bit machine: 64-bit pointers and FP64 (the D extension follows XLEN=64), with a 48-bit device address space against NVIDIA's 49-bit virtual addresses; configure --profile picks a build64 tree and a build32 tree rejects the profile
sources.NUM_BARRIERS: 16 named CTA barriers (bar.sync 0-15, PTX ISA) on every NVIDIA GPU
sources.EXT_RASTER_ENABLE, EXT_OM_ENABLE: Raster engines in every GPC and ROPs in every memory partition (architecture whitepaper)
sources.RTU_TLAS_ENABLE: RT cores traverse two-level acceleration structures (instance TLAS over BLAS), as DXR/Vulkan ray tracing requires
sources.NUM_MUFU_LANES: 16 special-function results per clock per SM (4 SFUs in each of the 4 processing blocks) for the reciprocal, reciprocal square root, log2, exp2, sine and cosine (CUDA C++ Programming Guide, arithmetic instruction throughput, compute capability 12.0)
sources.NUM_ALU_LANES, NUM_FPU_LANES, NUM_LSU_LA: GB203 SM (RTX Blackwell whitepaper, Figure 5 and App. B): 4 processing blocks, each with 32 unified FP32/INT32 CUDA cores (INT32 TOPS = FP32 TFLOPS, Table 4), 4 LD/ST units and 1 SFU, 1 tensor core; 2 FP64 cores per SM. One Vortex ALU/FPU/LSU block per processing block (ISSUE_WIDTH=4) with the part's INT32, FP32 and LD/ST lanes; a 32-thread warp instruction issues over NUM_THREADS/lanes cycles, as on the part. The TCU stays full-warp (NUM_TCU_LANES == NUM_THREADS). FP64 FMAs run on their own F64 FMA PE (FMA64_PE_RATIO)
sources.FMA64_PE_RATIO: FP64 FMA at 1/64 of the FP32 rate: 2 FP64 cores per SM, half a core per processing block (CUDA C++ Programming Guide, arithmetic instruction throughput, compute capability 12.0). A block keeps at least one PE, so 32 FPU lanes / 64 rounds up to 1 F64 FMA PE: 1/32 of FP32, twice the part's FP64 rate. FP64 division, square root and conversions take the FDIV/FSQRT/FCVT rates
sources.FDIV_PE_RATIO, FSQRT_PE_RATIO, FCVT_PE_R: 16 results per clock per SM, 4 per processing block: FP32 reciprocal and reciprocal square root, on which division and square root are built, and the 32-bit type conversions (CUDA C++ Programming Guide, arithmetic instruction throughput); 32 FPU lanes / 8, compute capability 12.0
sources.LMEM_SIZE, LMEM_LOG_SIZE, DCACHE_SIZE: 100 KB maximum shared memory per SM (compute capability 12.0 device query: 102400 B per SM) in a 128 KB window. DCACHE_SIZE keeps the whole 128 KB L1/shared pool: the driver gives a kernel the L1 its shared-memory use leaves
